name: Protocol Tunneling
description:
Adversaries may tunnel network communications to and from a victim system within a separate protocol to avoid detection/network filtering and/or enable access to otherwise unreachable systems. Tunneling involves explicitly encapsulating a protocol within another. This behavior may conceal malicious traffic by blending in with existing traffic and/or provide an outer layer of encryption (similar to a VPN). Tunneling could also enable routing of network packets that would otherwise not reach their intended destination, such as SMB, RDP, or other traffic that would be filtered by network appliances or not routed over the Internet. 

There are various means to encapsulate a protocol within another protocol. For example, adversaries may perform SSH tunneling (also known as SSH port forwarding), which involves forwarding arbitrary data over an encrypted SSH tunnel.(Citation: SSH Tunneling)(Citation: Sygnia Abyss Locker 2025) 

[Protocol Tunneling](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1572) may also be abused by adversaries during [Dynamic Resolution](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1568). Known as DNS over HTTPS (DoH), queries to resolve C2 infrastructure may be encapsulated within encrypted HTTPS packets.(Citation: BleepingComp Godlua JUL19) 

Adversaries may also leverage [Protocol Tunneling](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1572) in conjunction with [Proxy](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1090) and/or [Protocol or Service Impersonation](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1001/003) to further conceal C2 communications and infrastructure.

telemetry.name: Application Log Content
telemetry.description: Application-emitted audit or operational event content.
telemetry.collection_focus: Select the application event family required by the detection and document its native schema before normalization.

providers.name: Application audit logs
providers.scope: First-party service events and request/result fields; schema is application-specific.

providers.name: OpenTelemetry-compatible log pipelines
providers.scope: Transport and normalization of emitted records; do not create missing audit instrumentation.

configuration: Enable the application audit category or instrument the owned lab application at the authorization/action boundary.
Define a schema with timestamp, service, actor, object, action, result and correlation ID. Export structured records through an authenticated collector.
Redact secrets and personal content, separate audit from debug logs, set retention and verify delivery during rotation/restart.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Debug output is not necessarily a durable audit trail. Application developers must emit the relevant event; installing a log pipeline does not make an absent event exist.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per application, client and route: request rate, rare actions, failure ratios and unusual state transitions. Version changes, retries, health probes and seasonal load need separate baselines.

configuration: On a disposable Windows host, review the installed Sysmon schema and current configuration; merge scoped event filters into the existing policy rather than replacing it.

For Linux or macOS, select the equivalent sensor separately and test its emitted fields; a Windows event ID does not transfer across platforms.

telemetry.name: Network Traffic Content
telemetry.description: Packet or decoded application-protocol content visible at a network sensor.
telemetry.collection_focus: Scope approved packet capture/protocol content collection to the lab flow; retain capture provenance and truncation indicators.

providers.name: Zeek
providers.scope: Connection and protocol metadata from traffic visible to the sensor.

providers.name: Suricata EVE
providers.scope: Configured flow, alert, DNS, HTTP, TLS and protocol records.

configuration: Use an authorized lab TAP/SPAN, virtual mirror or gateway interface. Define which traffic crosses it; avoid assuming visibility into every segment.
Enable the required Zeek analyzers or Suricata EVE event types. Export logs with sensor identity, clock synchronization and flow correlation identifiers.
Monitor capture loss, truncation and exporter sampling. Capture payload only with approval and restrictive retention; encryption normally prevents plaintext inspection.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Flows are not packet payloads. NAT, asymmetric routes, encryption, missing mirrors and sampling can hide attribution or content. A destination connection alone does not prove malicious intent.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per source and observation point: connection rate, destination-host/port fan-out, response/failure ratio and previously unseen destinations. Compare equivalent time windows; separate authorized scanners, NAT and sampling effects.

strategies.name: Detection Strategy for Protocol Tunneling accross OS platforms.

analytics.name: Analytic 1483
analytics.guidance: Processes such as plink.exe, ssh.exe, or netsh.exe establishing outbound network connections where traffic patterns show encapsulated protocols (e.g., RDP over SSH). Defender observations include anomalous process-to-network relationships, large asymmetric data flows, and port usage mismatches.

tuning.description: Whitelist legitimate tunneling tools (e.g., used by admins).
Ratio of sent vs received bytes that indicates tunneling activity.
Correlate process creation with network connection within N seconds.

analytics.name: Analytic 1484
analytics.guidance: sshd, socat, or custom binaries initiating port forwarding or encapsulating traffic (e.g., RDP, SMB) through SSH or HTTP. Defender sees abnormal connect/bind syscalls, encrypted traffic on ports typically used for non-encrypted services, and outlier traffic volume patterns.

tuning.description: Specific sshd config flags indicating port forwarding.
Define expected application protocols by port to catch tunneling mismatches.

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: socket/connect calls showing SSH processes forwarding arbitrary ports

log_sources.name: linux:syslog
log_sources.channel: sshd sessions with unusual port forwarding parameters

log_sources.name: linux:osquery
log_sources.channel: socat, ssh, or nc processes opening unexpected ports

analytics.name: Analytic 1485
analytics.guidance: launchd or user-invoked processes (ssh, socat) encapsulating traffic via SSH tunnels, VPN-style tooling, or DNS-over-HTTPS clients. Defender sees outbound TLS traffic with embedded DNS or RDP payloads.

tuning.description: Known legitimate DoH resolvers used in environment.
Flag excessive randomness in payloads on standard ports.

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: process execution of ssh with -L/-R forwarding flags

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: encrypted outbound traffic carrying unexpected application data

analytics.name: Analytic 1486
analytics.guidance: VMware daemons or user processes encapsulating traffic (e.g., guest VMs tunneling via hostd). Defender sees network services inside ESXi creating flows inconsistent with management plane traffic, such as SSH forwarding or DNS-over-HTTPS from management interfaces.

tuning.description: Baseline allowed services and expected ports for ESXi management.

log_sources.name: esxi:vpxd
log_sources.channel: ESXi processes relaying traffic via SSH or unexpected ports

log_sources.name: esxcli:network
log_sources.channel: listening sockets bound with non-standard encapsulated protocols

candidates.name: DNS over HTTPS Regular Beaconing
candidates.description:
This test simulates an infected host beaconing via DoH queries to a command and control server at regular intervals over time.
This behaviour is typical of implants either in an idle state waiting for instructions or configured to use a low query volume over time to evade threshold based detection.
A custom domain and sub-domain will need to be passed as input parameters for this test to work. Upon execution, DNS information about the domain will be displayed for each callout in a JSON format.

runtime.description: Time in minutes to run the simulation

subdomain.description: Subdomain prepended to the domain name

c2_interval.description: Seconds between C2 requests to the command and control server

c2_jitter.description: Percentage of jitter to add to the C2 interval to create variance in the times between C2 requests

candidates.name: Cloudflare tunnels (Linux/macOS)
candidates.description:
Cloudflared can be used for exposing local development environment/services/files over the internet.
This atomic will generate a dev tunnel binding it to the local service running on the provided port.
Reference:
- [Cloudflared Docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/connections/connect-networks/)
- [LOT Tunnels](https://lottunnels.github.io/lottunnels/Binaries/cloudflared/)

additional_args.description: Additional arguments to pass to cloudflared

candidates.name: Install and Run gost Tunnel Proxy
candidates.description:
Downloads and runs gost (Go Simple Tunnel), a multi-protocol proxy and tunnel
tool used by adversaries to establish SOCKS5 proxies, protocol relays, and
encrypted tunnels on compromised hosts to facilitate C2 communication and
lateral movement while evading network controls.

remote_url.description: URL to download the gost release archive

gost_path.description: Path to store the gost binary

listen_port.description: Local port for the SOCKS5 proxy listener

candidates.name: run ngrok
candidates.description: Download and run ngrok. Create tunnel to chosen port.

candidates.name: DNS over HTTPS Long Domain Query
candidates.description:
This test simulates an infected host returning data to a command and control server using long domain names.
The simulation involves sending DoH queries that gradually increase in length until reaching the maximum length. The intent is to test the effectiveness of detection of DoH queries for long domain names over a set threshold.
 Upon execution, DNS information about the domain will be displayed for each callout in a JSON format.

subdomain.description: Subdomain prepended to the domain name (should be 63 characters to test maximum length)

candidates.name: Microsoft Dev tunnels (Linux/macOS)
candidates.description:
Dev Tunnels enables insiders as well as threat actors to expose local ports over the internet via Microsoft dev tunnels.

This atomic will generate a dev tunnel binding it to the local service running on the provided port. Can be used to expose local services, web applications and local files etc.
Reference:
- [Microsoft Docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/tunnels/dev-tunnels-overview)
- [LOT Tunnels](https://lottunnels.github.io/lottunnels/Binaries/devtunnels/)

candidates.name: DNS over HTTPS Large Query Volume
candidates.description:
This test simulates an infected host sending a large volume of DoH queries to a command and control server.
The intent of this test is to trigger threshold based detection on the number of DoH queries either from a single source system or to a single targe domain.
A custom domain and sub-domain will need to be passed as input parameters for this test to work. Upon execution, DNS information about the domain will be displayed for each callout in a JSON format.

subdomain.description: Subdomain prepended to the domain name

query_volume.description: Number of DNS queries to send

candidates.name: VSCode tunnels (Linux/macOS)
candidates.description:
Visual Studio Code Remote Tunnels can be used for exposing local development environment/services/files over the internet.
This atomic will generate a dev tunnel binding it to the local service running on the provided port.
Reference:
- [Microsoft Docs](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/remote/tunnels)
- [LOT Tunnels](https://lottunnels.github.io/lottunnels/Binaries/vscode-server/)

additional_args.description: additional arguments to pass to code tunnel

candidates.name: Install and Run frpc Reverse Proxy Client
candidates.description:
Downloads and runs frpc (fast reverse proxy client), the victim-side component
of the frp framework. Adversaries deploy frpc on compromised hosts to establish
outbound tunnel connections to an attacker-controlled frps server, bypassing
inbound firewall rules and exposing internal services externally.

remote_url.description: URL to download the frp release archive

frp_path.description: Path to extract the frp archive

server_addr.description: Address of the frps server to connect to

server_port.description: Port of the frps server to connect to
